name: Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole
executiveSummary: Co-trimoxazole. Dose by trimethoprim (TMP): usual adult 160 mg TMP every 12 h; pediatrics 8–12 mg/kg/day TMP every 12 h; PCP/severe disease 15–20 mg/kg/day TMP.
indications:
## Indications

- UTI due to susceptible organisms (*E. coli*, *Proteus*, *Klebsiella*, *Enterobacter*, *S. saprophyticus*, etc.).
- Acute otitis media due to susceptible *S. pneumoniae* / *H. influenzae* (not prolonged otitis prophylaxis).
- Treatment and prophylaxis of *Pneumocystis jirovecii* pneumonia; some *Stenotrophomonas* infections.

## Precautions

- Avoid under 2 months (kernicterus/immaturity) unless life-saving.
- Sulfonamide hypersensitivity, folate-deficiency megaloblastic anemia, severe renal failure: caution or contraindication per label.
- Interactions: warfarin, phenytoin, methotrexate, cyclosporine, rifampin.

> Always express and calculate dose by the **TMP component**.

adulto.presentation: Single-strength tablets 80/400 mg; double-strength (DS) 160/800 mg; syrup; ampoule 80 mg TMP + 400 mg SMX / 5 mL.
adulto.dose: Mild–moderate: **160 mg TMP / 800 mg SMX (1 DS) every 12 h** (usual max **640 mg TMP/day**). PCP / severe: **15–20 mg/kg/day TMP** divided every 6–8 h IV or PO. PCP prophylaxis: **160 mg TMP/day** or **160 mg 3×/week** per protocol. UTI prophylaxis: often **80–160 mg TMP at night**.
adulto.administration: PO with water; adequate hydration. IV: dilute 1 amp (80/400) in ≥ 100 mL NS or 5% dextrose (~0.8 mg/mL TMP); infuse 30–60 min (not > 90 min). Never undiluted.
adulto.notes: Common dilution: 1 mL concentrate in 5 mL diluent.

pediatrico.presentation: Tablets 80/400 and 160/800; syrup 40 mg TMP + 200 mg SMX / 5 mL; ampoules 80/400 / 5 mL.
pediatrico.dose: By **TMP**: mild–moderate **8–12 mg/kg/day every 12 h** (max **320 mg TMP/day**). Severe / PCP / *Stenotrophomonas* / meningitis: **20 mg/kg/day every 6 h** (max IV ~**240 mg TMP/dose** every 6 h; PO ~**320 mg/dose** every 6 h). PCP prophylaxis: **5 mg/kg/day TMP** 3×/week (max 160 mg). UTI prophylaxis: **2 mg/kg/day** TMP at night.
pediatrico.administration: PO/IV. Diluted IV ≥ 60 min with pump.
pediatrico.notes: Keep fixed 1:5 TMP:SMX ratio when measuring syrup.

neonatal.dose: Not routine under 2 months; life-saving indication only under NNU/ID with protocol dosing.

stability:
## Stability

- IV dilution: use promptly (usually ≤ 2 h at room temperature); prepare immediately before administration.
- Opened ampoule: discard remainder.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Rash (including severe SJS/TEN), nausea, vomiting, blood dyscrasias, nephrotoxicity, hepatitis/cholestasis, hyperkalemia.
